newsitem.title: CANADA: Chretien callS Chirac over De Gaulle stamp -report.
newsitem.headline: Chretien callS Chirac over De Gaulle stamp -report.

text.p: A Canadian newspaper said on Friday that Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien had telephoned French President Jacques Chirac to register concern over a proposed stamp that would appear to promote Quebec independence.

France is considering issuing a postage stamp commemorating former president Charles de Gaulle's controversial 1967 visit to Quebec, though a French spokesman said this week no decision had been made.
De Gaulle encouraged separatists, and enraged the Canadian federal government, by declaring "Vive le Quebec libre" (Long live a free Quebec) from the balcony of Montreal's city hall.
The Ottawa Citizen reported that Chretien called Chirac on Monday to seek more information about the stamp.
It said Chirac told Chretien he was not aware of the stamp, even though stories about it had appeared in the French media.
Ottawa is keen not to fuel separatist fire in Quebec, a mainly French-speaking province. A 1995 referendum on Quebec sovereignty lost by only one percentage point.
